s:
Arrange the following enactments in chronological order of their enactment:
A. Forest (Conservation) Act
B. Environment (Protection) Act
C. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
D. National Green Tribunal Act
x: The Water Act was enacted in 1974, the Forest (Conservation) Act in 1980, the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986 and the National Green Tribunal Act in 2010.
tq: Use the first and last items as anchors, then place the middle enactments by year.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s: Which one of the following was the first pollution-control law among the enactments listed below?
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
x: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, is described as India’s first pollution law and also created the pollution-control Boards.
tq: Identify the earliest specialised pollution statute rather than the later umbrella law.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 came into force on:
x: The Water Act came into force on 23 March 1974.
tq: Distinguish the commencement date from the year of enactment.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act:
1. It was enacted on 29 March 1981.
2. It came into force on 16 May 1981.
3. It followed the framework of the Water Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Air Act was enacted on 29 March 1981, commenced on 16 May 1981 and adopted the institutional framework of the Water Act.
tq: Check each date and the institutional relationship before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s: Which of the following pairs relating to amendments is correctly matched?
x: The Water Act was amended in 1988, while the Air Act was amended in 1987 and again in 1988.
tq: Pair each statute with its specific amendment years and reject shifted dates.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 primarily imposed a cess on water consumed by:
o: Agricultural farms and forest departments בלבד
x: The Water Cess Act imposed a cess on water consumed by industries and local bodies. The associated Cess Rules were made in 1978.
tq: Focus on the specified liable users instead of the broader group of water consumers.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal significance of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980?
o: It required Central approval for diversion of forest land.
It transferred all forests to local bodies.
It established the National Green Tribunal.
x: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 made Central approval necessary for diversion of forest land.
tq: Match the statute with its distinctive regulatory function rather than its subject in general terms.
sec: Environmental Acts - enactment chronology

s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is popularly known as an umbrella legislation because it:
o: creates only judicial authorities for environmental disputes
coordinates the Central and State authorities created under the Water and Air Acts
x: The Act provides an umbrella framework to coordinate the Central and State authorities established under the Water Act, 1974 and Air Act, 1981.
tq: Test the exact institutional meaning of a familiar descriptive term.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Which one of the following is the primary purpose of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: To regulate only the use of forest land
To protect and improve the environment and control pollution
To levy a cess on municipal water consumption
To establish a specialised environmental tribunal
x: The Act provides a framework for protecting and improving the environment and controlling pollution.
tq: Match the umbrella statute with its broad statutory purpose, not with a related specialised law.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the primary authority responsible for environmental protection is the:
x: The Central Government is the primary authority under the Environment (Protection) Act.
tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the statutory authority.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s:
Which of the following powers may be exercised by the Central Government under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
1. Laying down emission and discharge standards
2. Regulating the location of industries
3. Managing hazardous wastes
4. Protecting public health
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Central Government’s powers include prescribing emission and discharge standards, regulating industrial locations, managing hazardous wastes and protecting public health.
tq: Treat a comprehensive list of statutory powers as correct only after checking every item.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Directions issued by the Central Government under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 may include:
o: appointment of judges to the National Green Tribunal
dissolution of a State Legislative Assembly
x: Section 5 empowers the Central Government to issue directions, including directions for closure of an industrial unit.
tq: Separate an environmental executive direction from powers belonging to constitutional or judicial authorities.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The National Ganga River Basin Authority, constituted in 2009, is an example of an authority constituted under:
o: Section 5 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
Section 16 of the Water Cess Act, 1977
x: The National Ganga River Basin Authority was an authority constituted under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act.
tq: Use the section-number and body-name pairing to avoid confusing statutory authorities with constitutional bodies.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The Environment Protection Fund established under Section 16 of the Environment (Protection) Act is maintained in the:
o: Public Account of the State concerned only
x: The Environment Protection Fund under Section 16 is maintained in the Public Account.
tq: Discriminate between the three constitutional public-fund categories.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Environment Protection Fund:
1. It holds fines collected under the Air, Water and Environment Protection Acts.
2. Seventy-five per cent of the fund is allocated to States and Union Territories.
3. Twenty-five per cent is allocated to the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Fund receives fines under the three specified environmental laws, with 75% allocated to States and Union Territories and 25% to the Centre.
tq: Verify both the source of receipts and the percentage split before choosing the complete combination.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 were notified by the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The Environmental (Protection) Fund Rules, 2026 were notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
tq: Use the ‘which ministry handles this subject?’ test to reject neighbouring ministries.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Doon Valley notification was issued in 1989, not 1991. Revdanda Creek was also covered in 1989, while Dhanu Taluka was covered in 1991.
tq: Find the single shifted year in a list of closely related notifications.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The Doon Valley notification under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 prohibited industries that:
o: were located within 24 kilometres of the coast
used more than 24 metric tonnes of coal or fuel per day
x: The Doon Valley notification of 1989 prohibited industries burning more than 24 metric tonnes of coal or fuel a day.
tq: Distinguish the threshold figure and its subject from nearby location-based restrictions.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Revdanda Creek notification?
o: It permitted industries only after coastal ash dumping.
It prohibited industries around the creek.
It authorised power plants in ecologically fragile areas.
It introduced voluntary tree planting credits.
x: The Revdanda Creek notification of 1989 prohibited industries around the creek.
tq: Match the place-specific notification with its precise restriction.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The Coastal Regulation Zone notification issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 primarily:
o: regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash or waste dumping
requires prior clearance for all forest diversion
x: The CRZ notification of 1991 regulates coastal stretches and prohibits ash and waste dumping in the regulated areas.
tq: Connect the environmental zone with its geographical subject and specific restriction.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the Dhanu Taluka notification?
o: It imposed a cess on water consumed by industries.
It declared the area ecologically fragile and prohibited power plants.
It established Central Pollution Control Boards.
It permitted unrestricted industrial development in coastal stretches.
x: The Dhanu Taluka notification of 1991 identified the area as ecologically fragile and prohibited power plants there.
tq: Use the location-specific restriction to distinguish the notification from other environmental instruments.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The Environmental Impact Assessment notification under the Environment (Protection) Act is associated with:
x: The EIA notification was issued in 1994 and was subsequently revised in 2006; it provides for prior environmental clearance.
tq: Pair the original notification year with its later revision and the clearance requirement.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Prior environmental clearance is principally associated with which notification under the Environment (Protection) Act?
x: The EIA notification, first issued in 1994 and revised in 2006, provides for prior environmental clearance.
tq: Match the administrative requirement with the notification specifically designed for it.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s:
Which of the following instruments has been notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
1. Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications
2. Plastic Waste Management Rules
3. Green Credit Rules
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Eco-Sensitive Zone notifications, the Plastic Waste Management Rules and the Green Credit Rules are all instruments notified under the Environment (Protection) Act.
tq: Test whether the listed instruments belong to the umbrella Act rather than to a specialised statute.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Under the Green Credit Rules, 2023, voluntary tree planting on degraded land can earn:
x: The Green Credit Rules, 2023 provide Green Credits for voluntary tree planting on degraded land.
tq: Match the environmental action with the exact official incentive term.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: Which one of the following statements regarding standards under the Environment (Protection) Act is correct?
o: The Central Pollution Control Board publishes standards without any Central Ministry involvement.
Standards are notified only by the National Green Tribunal.
Standards are issued exclusively by local municipal bodies.
Standards are published in the Gazette by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change with the Central Pollution Control Board.
x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, in association with the Central Pollution Control Board, publishes standards in the Gazette.
tq: Identify the correct institutional partnership instead of assigning the function to a neighbouring authority.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The lead content in paints was capped at which level as an example of a standard under the Environment (Protection) Act?
x: Lead in paints was capped at 90 parts per million as an example of a standard published under the Act.
tq: Handle a numerical scale trap by checking the order of magnitude of the stated limit.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: What was the original maximum punishment provided under the Environment (Protection) Act for an offence?
o: Only a written warning issued by the Central Government
Up to 5 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 1 lakh, with Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence
Life imprisonment and forfeiture of all property
Up to 2 years’ imprisonment or a fine of Rs 10,000, with no continuing penalty
x: The original penalty was imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to Rs 1 lakh, with an additional Rs 5,000 per day for a continuing offence.
tq: Read the full penalty structure, including the continuing-offence component, rather than only the headline punishment.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act was decriminalised through the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977
x: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised the penalty regime under the Environment (Protection) Act.
tq: Distinguish the original criminal penalty provisions from their later legislative modification.
sec: EPA 1986 - trigger, umbrella nature, powers, authorities, rules and notifications

s: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 primarily seeks to:
o: Control the use of genetically modified organisms
Protect forests and wildlife through protected-area management
Regulate only the discharge of industrial effluents into rivers
Prevent, control and abate air pollution and maintain air-quality standards
x: The principal objective of the Air Act is to prevent, control and abate air pollution and to maintain prescribed air-quality standards.
tq: Identify the precise statutory purpose rather than a related environmental objective.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Air Act, 1981:
1. It came into force on 16 May 1981.
2. It consists of seven chapters and 54 sections.
3. It was modelled on the Water Act, 1974.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Air Act came into force on 16 May 1981, contains seven chapters and 54 sections, and was modelled on the Water Act.
tq: Split the options by checking the date, structure and legislative relationship separately.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following was specifically added to the definition of ‘air pollutant’ by the 1987 amendment to the Air Act?
x: The 1987 amendment expanded the definition of air pollutant to include noise.
tq: Discriminate between the statutory definition of air pollutant and other environmental pollutants.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: Who is empowered to declare an area as an air pollution control area under the Air Act, 1981?
x: The State Government may declare an air pollution control area under Chapter IV, particularly Sections 19 to 31, of the Air Act.
tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the competent authority.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: Section 31A of the Air Act, 1981 is associated with the power to:
o: Give directions for enforcement of the Act
Collect water cess from local authorities
x: Section 31A empowers the pollution control authorities to issue directions, including directions connected with enforcement and environmental compensation.
tq: Match the section number with its distinctive statutory power.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The CPCB was already in existence under the Water Act before it was assigned functions under the Air Act.
2. State Pollution Control Boards enforce the provisions of the Air Act at the State level.
3. The Air Act created an entirely separate set of Central and State Boards unrelated to the Water Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The CPCB, originally established under the Water Act, was assigned air-pollution functions, while SPCBs enforce the Act in the States. Statement 3 is false because the same board structure was used.
tq: Spot the wrong statement that reverses the institutional relationship between the two Acts.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Water Act, 1974 from the Air Act, 1981?
o: The Water Act has eight chapters and 64 sections, whereas the Air Act has seven chapters and 54 sections.
The Water Act has seven chapters and 54 sections, whereas the Air Act has eight chapters and 64 sections.
Both Acts have eight chapters and 64 sections.
Both Acts have seven chapters and 54 sections.
x: The Water Act contains eight chapters and 64 sections; the Air Act contains seven chapters and 54 sections.
tq: Compare the numerical structure of the two statutes without reversing the columns.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Act)
a. Water Act, 1974
b. Air Act, 1981
c. Water Cess Act, 1977

d. Air Act amendment, 1987

List-II (Feature)
i. Inclusion of noise in the definition of air pollutant
 ii. Cess on water consumed by specified industries and local authorities
 iii. Standards for discharge of effluents
 iv. Declaration of air pollution control areas and emission standards

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Water Act deals with effluent-discharge standards; the Air Act deals with air-control areas and emissions; the Cess Act funds the Boards; and the 1987 amendment added noise.
tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a reversed statutory feature.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is a common requirement under both the Water Act, 1974 and the Air Act, 1981?
o: Compulsory registration under the Water Cess Act
Declaration of every industrial site as an air pollution control area
Prior consent of the concerned Board to establish and operate a polluting unit
Prior approval of the National Green Tribunal for every industrial unit
x: Both Acts require prior consent of the Pollution Control Board for establishing and operating a unit that may cause pollution.
tq: Find the common legal mechanism rather than a feature belonging exclusively to one Act.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: The power of Pollution Control Boards to levy environmental compensation under Section 31A of the Air Act and Section 33A of the Water Act was upheld subject to which limitation?
o: It may be exercised without any connection to actual or imminent harm.
It may be exercised only against government-owned industries.
It may be exercised only when environmental harm is clear or imminent.
It may be exercised only after a criminal conviction.
x: The power to levy compensation has been upheld, but its exercise must be connected with clear or imminent environmental harm.
tq: Apply the legal power to a fact pattern while checking the limiting condition.
sec: Air Act 1981 - purpose, noise, air pollution control areas  [APPSC]

s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 is regarded as India’s first:
x: The Water Act, 1974 is regarded as India’s first pollution-control law and focuses on preventing and controlling water pollution.
tq: Recall the distinctive historical position of the statute among environmental laws.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s: The Water Act, 1974 was enacted under Article 252 of the Constitution. What is the implication of this arrangement?
o: It applies to States that adopt it through the constitutionally prescribed process.
It can be enforced only after approval by the Supreme Court.
It automatically applies only to Union Territories.
It applies exclusively to subjects in the Union List.
x: Article 252 permits Parliament to legislate on a State subject when States adopt the required resolution; the law applies in the States adopting it.
tq: Connect the constitutional route of legislation with its territorial application.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s: Which body was renamed the Central Pollution Control Board by the 1988 amendment to the Water Act?
o: Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution
x: The Central Board for the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution, created in 1974, was renamed the CPCB by the 1988 amendment.
tq: Use the predecessor-to-present-name relationship to avoid confusing neighbouring water institutions.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s:
Before discharging effluents, an industry generally requires:
1. Consent to establish from the State Pollution Control Board
2. Consent to operate from the State Pollution Control Board
3. Permission only from the National Green Tribunal

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Industries require consent to establish and consent to operate from the SPCB before discharging effluents. Permission only from the NGT is not the statutory consent mechanism.
tq: Reject the wrong-authority trap by identifying the body that grants operational consent.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s: The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977 was intended primarily to:
o: Raise funds for the Pollution Control Boards through a cess on specified water consumption
Replace the consent mechanism under the Water Act
Impose a cess exclusively on agricultural land holdings
x: The Cess Act imposed a cess on water consumed by specified industries and local authorities to finance the activities of the Boards.
tq: Identify the funding purpose and reject unrelated environmental-finance functions.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s: Under the Water Cess Act, a rebate of 25 per cent was available for installing:
x: The Water Cess Act provided a 25 per cent rebate for installing treatment plants, encouraging reduction and treatment of polluted discharges.
tq: Link the numerical rebate with the specific compliance measure it encouraged.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements about the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act, 1977:
1. Its proceeds were credited to the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. It contained 17 sections.
3. It was subsumed or repealed in connection with the introduction of GST in 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Cess Act had 17 sections, its proceeds went to the Consolidated Fund of India, and it was subsumed or repealed with the GST framework in 2017.
tq: Check each independent statutory detail before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Water Rules were made in 1975, while the Cess Rules were made in 1978.
tq: Distinguish the close years attached to the Water Rules and Cess Rules.
sec: Water Act 1974 - purpose, boards, consent, Cess Act link  [APPSC]

s: The ‘polluter pays’ principle means that:
o: Pollution is permissible if compensation is paid in advance.
The State must bear all costs of environmental restoration irrespective of the polluter.
Only affected residents must finance environmental restoration.
The person or company responsible for pollution bears the cost of repairing the resulting damage.
x: Under the polluter-pays principle, the responsible person or company bears the cost of repairing environmental damage caused by the pollution.
tq: Apply the exact meaning of a legal principle to the responsible party and the remedial cost.
sec: Judicial principles → case  [APPSC]

s: Which case is associated with the introduction of both the precautionary principle and the polluter-pays principle into Indian environmental law?
o: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India
M.C. Mehta v Union of India concerning the Oleum gas leak
Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India
x: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India, decided in 1996, is associated with both the precautionary and polluter-pays principles. Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action reaffirmed polluter pays.
tq: Use the case-principle association rather than matching all cases by environmental subject alone.
sec: Judicial principles → case  [APPSC]

s: Under the precautionary principle, environmental harm should be prevented:
o: Only when the developer voluntarily accepts liability
Only after the harm has become irreversible
Only when a criminal court first establishes negligence
Even when complete scientific certainty about the harm is unavailable
x: The precautionary principle requires preventive action despite the absence of complete scientific certainty, and the burden of proof lies on the developer.
tq: Recognise the preventive logic of the principle and reject the ‘wait for certainty’ trap.
sec: Judicial principles → case  [APPSC]

s: The doctrine of absolute liability for hazardous industries is associated with:
o: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India
Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India
M.C. Mehta v Union of India concerning the Oleum gas leak
x: The Oleum gas leak case established absolute liability for hazardous industries, without the exceptions traditionally associated with strict liability.
tq: Match the distinctive judicial principle with the case involving hazardous industry liability.
sec: Judicial principles → case  [APPSC]

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Precautionary principle — Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India
Public trust doctrine — M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath
Absolute liability — M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath
Polluter pays — Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India
x: Absolute liability is associated with M.C. Mehta v Union of India in the Oleum gas leak case. M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath is associated with the public trust doctrine.
tq: Find the single swapped case-principle pair.
sec: Judicial principles → case  [APPSC]

s: The right to a clean and pollution-free environment has been read by the Supreme Court into:
x: The Supreme Court has interpreted the right to life under Article 21 to include the right to a healthy, clean and pollution-free environment.
tq: Identify the constitutional article through the judicially expanded right rather than its literal wording alone.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s: Article 48A of the Constitution directs the State to:
o: Establish a separate Pollution Control Board in every district
Protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife
Impose a fundamental duty on every citizen to protect rivers
Guarantee free legal aid in environmental disputes
x: Article 48A is a Directive Principle requiring the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.
tq: Separate a Directive Principle addressed to the State from a Fundamental Duty addressed to citizens.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s: Which of the following is included in the Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(g)?
o: Protecting and improving the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife
Constituting the Central Pollution Control Board
x: Article 51A(g) requires citizens to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to show compassion for living creatures.
tq: Distinguish a citizen’s environmental duty from statutory functions of public authorities.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 48A and 51A(g) were inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
2. Article 48A is a Directive Principle of State Policy.
3. Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The 42nd Amendment inserted Article 48A as a Directive Principle and Article 51A(g) as a Fundamental Duty, both in 1976.
tq: Check the amendment, constitutional part and article classification together.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s:
Assertion (A): Article 21 has been interpreted to include the right to a healthy environment.
Reason (R): The right to life under Article 21 is not confined to mere physical existence.

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both statements are true. The broad judicial interpretation of the right to life beyond mere physical existence supports inclusion of a healthy environment within Article 21.
tq: Test whether the constitutional explanation directly supports the judicial interpretation.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s: Which constitutional provision has been linked by the Supreme Court with enforcement action by Pollution Control Boards?
x: The Supreme Court has linked Pollution Control Board enforcement to the citizen’s environmental duty under Article 51A(g).
tq: Use the specific constitutional linkage instead of selecting a generally environment-related provision.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. Enactment of the Water Cess Act
B. Enactment of the Air Act
C. 42nd Constitutional Amendment inserting Articles 48A and 51A(g)
D. Amendment to the Air Act adding noise to the definition of air pollutant
x: The sequence is Water Cess Act (1977), Air Act (1981), 42nd Amendment (1976) — wait, this ordering reveals that the constitutional amendment preceded the Air Act. Therefore the correct chronological sequence is C, A, B, D.
tq: Check the dates of the middle events carefully before fixing the sequence.
sec: Constitutional provisions - Articles 21, 48A, 51A(g)  [APPSC]

s: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 amended which environmental legislation referred to as the PLI Act, 1991?
x: The PLI Act mentioned in this context is the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, which was amended by the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023.
tq: Expand the exact abbreviation instead of choosing a look-alike statutory title.
sec: Jan Vishwas Act 2023 - decriminalised environmental provisions

s:
With reference to the environmental provisions amended by the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, consider the following statements:
1. Certain offences under the PLI Act, 1991 were decriminalised.
2. Imprisonment was replaced by monetary penalties for the offences concerned.
3. The Act transferred all environmental restoration responsibilities from CPCB and SPCBs to private insurers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The amendment decriminalised specified offences and substituted penalties for imprisonment. It did not transfer all restoration responsibilities to private insurers.
tq: Reject the extreme transfer-of-responsibility statement and identify the two linked legal changes.
sec: Jan Vishwas Act 2023 - decriminalised environmental provisions

s: Under the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, the Central Government may provide money from the Environmental Relief Fund to which bodies for restoration purposes?
x: The Central Government may provide Environmental Relief Fund money to the Central Pollution Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards for restoration.
tq: Match the statutory fund with the bodies authorised to use it.
sec: Jan Vishwas Act 2023 - decriminalised environmental provisions

s: The relief payable in cases involving death was raised to what amount under the Jan Vishwas-related amendment?
x: The relief for death was increased from ₹25,000 to ₹5 lakh.
tq: Distinguish the revised figure from the earlier compensation amount.
sec: Jan Vishwas Act 2023 - decriminalised environmental provisions

s: Which one of the following correctly describes another feature of the Jan Vishwas amendment referred to in relation to the PLI Act, 1991?
o: Environmental offences were made punishable only by imprisonment.
The Environmental Relief Fund was dissolved.
Penalty rates were shifted to rules.
x: The penalty rates were shifted to rules, while the amendment also replaced specified criminal consequences with penalties.
tq: Use the precise legal change rather than an absolute statement about abolition of penalties.
sec: Jan Vishwas Act 2023 - decriminalised environmental provisions

s: The Supreme Court judgment in Vanashakti v. Union of India primarily concerned the validity of:
o: The appointment of SPCB chairpersons by State Governments
Retrospective environmental clearances granted through a 2021 Office Memorandum
The creation of the National Air Quality Index
The classification of industries into red and orange categories
x: The Supreme Court nullified the 2021 Office Memorandum that permitted retrospective environmental clearances on payment of penalties.
tq: Identify the legal issue directly associated with the named case.
sec: Environment-related cases in news - M.C. Mehta, Vellore and others

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vanashakti v. Union of India case:
1. The Supreme Court held that administrative orders cannot override the EIA Notification, 2006.
2. The ruling on retrospective environmental clearance was prospective.
3. Ex post facto environmental clearance may be granted in every case merely on payment of a penalty.

tq: Find the false absolute statement using the phrase “every case”.
